items.problem: First dotnet build FAILED with CS0227 because the scaffold csproj did not enable unsafe code, while the AudioGraph frame-buffer source (IMemoryBufferByteAccess / byte* in CustomEffect.cs and Scenario3_FrameInputNode.xaml.cs) requires `unsafe`.
items.evidence: Migration session-log ~turn 46 build output (CS0227 in CustomEffect.cs and Scenario3_FrameInputNode.xaml.cs); fixed ~turn 47 by adding <AllowUnsafeBlocks>true</AllowUnsafeBlocks>.
items.covered_at: MIGRATION-PATTERNS.md, section '### CS0227: Unsafe code may only appear if compiling with /unsafe' — instructs adding <AllowUnsafeBlocks>true</AllowUnsafeBlocks>.
items.proposed_improvement: The guidance is purely reactive ('fix them inline as you encounter them'), so it only helps AFTER a failed build. Make it proactive at Tier 1: have Initialize-UwpMigration.ps1 scan the copied .cs for the `unsafe` keyword and, when present, auto-add <AllowUnsafeBlocks>true</AllowUnsafeBlocks> to the scaffold csproj during bootstrap; cross-reference this in the CS0227 note.
items.generalizes: Any UWP SDK sample that touches raw pixel/audio/media buffers (AudioGraph FrameInputNode, custom IBasicAudioEffect, SoftwareBitmap/pixel access, camera frames) compiles `unsafe`. The scaffold never enables it, so CS0227 recurs across the whole media-sample family. Auto-enabling at bootstrap removes a guaranteed build round-trip for that class.
